## How the orbit view is built (state at 03:45 UTC Nov 21)

- `globe.ts`: stop-local impostor. A back-side shell of radius 1.3, ray-sphere in the fragment shader, analytic limb coverage (clean at every tier, no haze, no glow at the limb from air). Shade = (curve(ndl) - night) x limb(mu) x relief lift + night. `curve.json` holds both tables, measured from the hero by `wrap/curve.py`: the hero brightens up to 2.46 times toward the lit limb (mu below 0.5), separate from the ndl curve.
- Lens glow outside the lit limb is a film layer in the same shader (the sky slides behind the globe in the hold, so it cannot live in the sky patch). It follows curve(dot(limb normal, Sun-in-sky direction projected on the image plane)), gated by the light on the limb. Hero glow is centered on position angle about 68 degrees (toward the Sun in frame), not on the light vector (57 degrees).
- `sunplate.ts`: the Sun is stop-local. The engine Sun cannot match the hero (flat pale disc, core dot, wide glow), so `sunGlare` is 0.012 and a sky-fixed additive plate draws the hero Sun (hero pixels plus two outpaints to complete the disc), fixed to the hold camera at holdMid, breathing with a sine that is zero at holdMid. In the arriving travel it fades in with smooth(ramp(0.25, 0.8, u)), the same ramp the engine uses for the Sun's glare; in the leaving travel it fades out with the same ramp. The plate carries no stars (polar low-percentile smoothing past 1.2 Sun radii).
- Sky patch `sky-hold.webp` (3520x1980 full, half for web, gain 4 with skyExposure 0.25): hero sky with the planet removed, minus the Sun plate, minus the film's bloom (frame 615 rendered with the rim glow off and a black sky patch). Hero stars kept between 1.012 and 1.3 radii on a star-free filled background, so no rim glow is baked in the sky.
- Wrap v1: `wrap/guide.py` (real mosaic graded to the hero's albedo statistics) then `wrap/match.py` (hero-2x pixels divided by the fitted shade, faded out between view cosine 0.42 and 0.2, tone ratio carried to the limb). The far side is still the unpainted guide.

## Terrain plan

- Engine class `Relief.load(ctx, base, def, motion)` in a `terrain` group as `src/stops/mars/set.ts`; `ReliefDef` {imageSize, vfovDeg, layers [{color, alpha?, dist, box, distSize, tint}], masks, maskBox, mistDir}; dist files raw float32 at half the layer size; masks black (no mist, no dust on Mercury).
- Distance = fit of 1 / (a x depth^g + b) to a sphere ground model from the camera fit. One layer first; a cut layer only if a sweep shows stretching. Margins outpainted about 12 percent left, right, bottom. Sky cut by alpha at the horizon.
- Terrain sky patch from the close image's sky (stars, Sun bloom at top left near x 730, y 10 of 2816x1584, glow along the horizon). `skyAim: { terrain: [...] }` in `plan.ts`.

## Decisions

- Terrain: spot near the terminator, light about 8 degrees above the local horizon, heading = light azimuth turned 26 degrees right, horizon tilt about 10.7 degrees, dip about 6.8 degrees at vfov 60. The terrain Sun comes from the terrain sky patch.
- Cover: engine cover as a warm flash plus stop-local glare streaks in `near`.
- Mars open items to avoid: covers that read as a cut, stepped disc edge, razor night limb, smeared far side, blown areas, no soft terminator in the rise, soft shadowed foreground, hard horizon glow edge, repeated patterns.

## Engine facts that matter here

- Render order: sky, `world`, `near` (depth cleared), dust, cover. Camera at the origin; the world group sits at origin minus camera with `state.rotation`.
- Sky patches: replace mode, coords = aim^-1 x world ray, orbit aim = frame rotation x hold camera at frame 615. Patch weight 1 in hold, dive, terrain; 0 for the orbit patch in the rise; arriving travel smoothstep(u, 0.2, 0.8); leaving travel 0.
- Travel from the Sun (index 0): the Sun set fades out and the engine Sun fades in over u 0.3 to 0.42 at Mercury's `sunRadiusDeg`; glare mixes to Mercury's value over u 0.25 to 0.8.
- `plan.sunDir` (where the Sun is drawn) comes from `fit.sunInFrame`; `plan.lightDir` shades the globe. They are 62 degrees apart in the hero.
- Post: bloom 6 levels, filmic, vignette, grain, sharpen. Stills: `npm run still -- --frame N --tier T --out FILE [--diag nograin]`.

The mesh interpolates it linearly, the horizon is tilted 11 degrees against the rows, so every row crossing made a tooth as soon as the camera left the fit pose (entry height 1 camera height: 0.6 heights of error at 11 heights is 9 px). Now the distance within 8 px of the horizon (plus the margin drop) is the tangent line of the sphere's profile, continued 10 px above the horizon, then constant. Linear in the image, so the mesh carries it exactly. `python3 assets-src/mercury/relief/build.py dist` writes only `relief-dist.bin` (both sets) from `out/work/mercury/relief/relief-detail.npy`. Your polish branch f269a9b stays as it is for Phase 6."

The critic on 495 (1400 px wide copy; multiply by 1.371 for 1920):
- major: "a faint greenish-grey horizontal streak floats in empty space, detached from the corona; it looks like a stray sprite or lens-flare leftover" (left of the star's limb, about x 600 to 720, y 225 to 240). Fix named: "remove the streak, or if it is meant to be a flare, tie it to the light source with a matching hue and falloff".
- major: "the photosphere is a soft, airbrushed swirl of noise; at native size there is no crisp granulation or sunspot detail and the texture looks smeared, like a blurred procedural layer" (disc surface). Fix named: "add a sharper granulation layer at small scale, with some limb darkening and a few defined active regions".
- major: "red prominences are thin, saturated red squiggles laid over the glow; they have no emission glow, no thickness and a different colour from the corona, so they read as painted strokes on a separate layer" (left limb and upper right limb). The Sun stop's prominences over my pale plate; sun_builder has them (MAIL 109 B).
- minor: "the coronal loops and radial spikes look like repeated brush-stroke sprites of similar size spaced evenly round the limb" (lower limb and the left limb's spikes).
- minor: "the galaxies are tiny orange blurred ellipses that are softer than the stars around them, like upscaled sprites" (two small smudges, x 435, y 530). On the motion sheet an orange dot drifts at the lower left from 499 to 539. "If these are your lens ghosts, they read as sprites, not as lens."
- motion critic, same stretch (6 of 10): "the Sun blows out from textured orange granulation to flat white while its orange Milky Way backdrop vanishes (474-499)".

"What I want from you, in this order:
1. The streak. It is the anamorphic streak seen only where it leaves the corona, so it reads as a separate grey bar. Make it one piece with its source: the hue of the disc's glare (warm white, no green), brightest at the disc and falling off outward, running through the glare instead of starting beside it. If that cannot be had at 495, fade the streak in later in the travel so it is not seen alone. Tell me the cause in one line (hue, mask, order of layers).
2. The plate's surface at native size at 495 and at your hold. The kit's tone rule: "Highlights roll off. They do not clip to flat white." The disc needs fine structure a viewer can find at 1:1 (granulation scale, a few active regions, limb darkening) under the glare, without changing your hold's match: frame 615 against the approved hero must stay as good as it is (send the 615 crop of the Sun's corner before and after beside the approved crop).
3. The loops and spikes round the pale limb: vary size, brightness and spacing, soften the spike ends into the glow.
4. The orange smudges: say what they are. If lens ghosts, either give them the look of a lens (a defined aperture shape with a soft rim, lying on the line through the frame centre opposite the Sun) or take them out of the travel.
sun_builder is changing the hand over itself (MAIL 109 B): its globe is to rise in exposure until it clips to your plate's look, and only then your plate takes over, so no doubled Sun at 482 and no red lines at 495. You two share the join: tell me what your plate's disc size, centre and level are at 488 to 499 so I can pass it on, or write to /root/sun_builder direct and copy me.

Proof I need (render on your VM, one process at a time): finals of 495 and 615 before and after with native crops of the streak, the disc surface, the limb loops and the smudges; a draft strip of 474 to 539 every fifth frame; a line that every other judged frame of your stop keeps its bytes at final (list which you rendered). ## MAIL 275 (23 Nov, 13:14 UTC, from the Builder, high, to every stop builder and coder): how a stop gets to its critic rounds

Word for word:

"From the Builder (/root) to every stop builder and coder. Mail 275: how your stop gets to its critic rounds. No answer needed unless a point below is red for you.

1. A stop is taken onto main and its round 1 starts (rounds are numbered on from 37, up to three per stop, every critic each round) when four things hold on one commit that you name:
 a. both handovers run with no cover and read as one place (Jupiter and Saturn: also the surface view from code; the Sun: the surface view with its new motion and the rise);
 b. the machine checks are green on every frame you changed: G5, G13 and G17 as the harness gives them, and the handover report of `npm run handover -- --stop <id>`;
 c. the frames you may not change keep their bytes (your hold and your surface view where it is approved, at the draft tier everywhere and at the final tier on the judged frames);
 d. build, tsc and tests are green on a merge of the newest main.
 It does not have to be finished. What is still wrong goes to the critics with the rest. Do not wait for a perfect state: when a to d hold, send me "READY <stop> <commit>" with the list of what you still see as wrong.
2. Takes of generated assets: kit/06-ASSETS.md gives six takes per asset per round, and six per phase for an asset made outside a round. A mail of mine with findings is not a round. If an asset has used its six in this phase, keep its best take and say so in your READY line. In a round each asset has six again where a critic asks for a change. Work by code has no take limit.
3. I render every commit you name at every frame on the render machines and write what I see. Push your code branch whenever your looks show something you want judged, and name the commit."

## 16:00 to 17:10 UTC: the four sided patch 738 to 743, cause and cure by code

Cause (measured with `--diag beauty/noplace`, `beauty/mask`, `beauty/picture` and tools `where.py`, `edgeprof.py`, `frameedge.py`): the terrain itself ends close to the T frame. In frame px beyond the T frame: left 37 (near) to 69 (far), right 46 to 50, bottom 19 at column 20, 30 at 200, 48 at 500, 67 at 800, 110 at 1400. The terrain darkens over its last 32 to 40 source px. The old field of the plates (border 160 source px) ended at about the T frame, so under the margin of the place picture the plate carried other ground than the picture, and the feather of the engine blended unlike ground along a straight line: the outline.

Cure, all in my folders:
- `mosaic.py`, `plates.py`, `plates.json mask.borderPx` 64: the field of the plates reaches to 64 source px before the terrain end (24 gave a dark line, the terrain is dark there).
- `plan.ts` dive `valid` [0.004, 0.004, 0.0045, 0.125] (8, 8, 5 px outside the T frame, inside the field everywhere), `edgeIn` [0.4, 0.4, 0.4, 0.25] on dive and rise.
- `band.py spill`: outside the field the plate takes ground copied from 1 degree further in (whole px shift, so it stays as sharp as its source; the bilinear shift before made it 35 percent softer by the Laplacian), led over to the picture at the junction by a membrane in a gamma 2.4 space (capped, short reach) with the first px exact.
- `band.py seam` and `kept`: the junction between the picture and the copied ground is no longer the straight field edge. A minimum cut (scipy maximum_flow on the px graph) between the field edge and the outer edge of the place picture (T frame plus `keepPx`) picks the line where picture and copy differ least. Found at level 4, saved as `seam-<kind>.npy`, used by all levels (band.py now lays the levels from 4 down).

Variants looked at and dropped: mirror at the edge (a spine with chevrons), crossfade of the plate into the picture margin (seam still at 743), border 24 (dark line), bilinear shift (soft copy), seam at half resolution (a dotted chain along the staircase), exact first 6 px (coloured comb).

Limits that stay: on the left and right side of the T frame the room for the seam is only 13 to 45 frame px (the tiles and the terrain end there), so the seam can dodge small forms only. At the far left the field ends with the cover of the tiles (lay weight), not with the terrain.

## MAIL 311 from /root, 18:03 UTC, to every stop builder (verbatim, binding)

Decision d129, engine part E6 (handover_engineer builds it now).

What: in the dives and rises of a stop that opted in, the shutter of a frame is shortened so that the motion across it is at most 6 px at the point of the frame that moves most (config handover.maxBlurPx), eased back to the full shutter over the last 12 frames of a rise. Every other frame of the film keeps the full shutter.

Why: the critics of rounds 37 and 40 score the judged dive and rise frames as smear, severe (Earth 1857 "extreme radial zoom blur and low resolution stretching, blocky stepped streaks", Earth 2156 "dragged into parallel streaks and do not hold detail at native size", Mercury 1016 "smeared into long directional streaks"). The motion across the full shutter is 25 to 80 px there, because one steady move changes scale by 6 to 14 percent a frame. The path cannot be slower, so the shutter is shorter.

What it means for you:
1. Do not slow or bend your path to get less blur and do not build a blur cure of your own.
2. From the next round your judged dive and rise frames (Sun 247; Mercury 717, 1016; Venus 1287, 1586; Earth 1857, 2156; Mars 2427, 2726; Jupiter 2997, 3296; Saturn 3567, 3866; Uranus 4137, 4436; Neptune 4707, 5006) and every frame of the motion sheets are nearly as sharp as your draft frames. Every fault the blur hid will be seen: plate edges, a level that pops, thin texture, clouds as blobs, the place picture as a patch, a halo at the limb. Look at those two frames at the draft tier at native size (crops of about 700 px, not the whole frame resized) and put what you find on your list, worst first.
3. Nothing to merge yet. I tell you when E6 is on main.
No answer needed.

## The pace step (plan E in my own path), 22:31 to 23:10 sandbox clock

What it is. Each dive and each rise is one path from the far end (the hold going on at 690, the travel's own pose at 1035) to the terrain's own flight at 780 and 960. - `set.ts`: time knobs key on the new frames of the change of view; the spin calls `plan.rested`; the surface glare is `shine(time, side)`, one function of height on both sides of the change of view; the halo of the limb is a function of the log of the height between the change of view and the terrain's end (no frames).

## Plan F step 3: the sphere under and round the relief in the close view, 23:12 to 23:50 sandbox clock

What it is. The close view drew only the relief meshes (ground and the wide mesh under it) on the limb plate and the sky, so wherever the frame looked past the edge of the meshes there was nothing. Now the planet itself stands under them: a second instance of the globe (`shell`), with the same plates, light and grade as the globe of the orbit view at the same moment, drawn in the close scene before the meshes.

- `set.ts`: `globeOf()` builds the two instances; `shell.mesh` sits in the `terrain` group after limb and rim (renderOrder -3), scale `closeRadius`, centre at `nearUp * -(closeRadius + 1)`, turn `toClose` (the anchor frame's inverse times the fit's globe turn), spin 0. `paint()` holds every per frame setter of the globe, so both instances are fed by one function. In the close view of a dive or a rise the set asks the film for the same moment drawn from the orbit side (`film.shotAt(frame, time, 'orbit')`), takes that side's light, Sun, glare Sun and line, turns them by `toLow` (close camera turn times the inverse of the orbit camera turn) and paints the shell with them.
- Presence is a function of height, not of the segment: `smoothstep(height, floor, floor + look.under.span)`, `floor` the larger of the terrain's own heights at its two ends (0.3017 close units over the camera's rest height), `span` 0.45. Full at and above 0.75 (frame 764 in the dive, 972 in the rise), nothing at and below the terrain's heights, so 780 to 959 keep their bytes and 779 to 780 and 959 to 960 show no step.
- The shell's silhouette is sunk by `look.under.sink` 0.283 close units (the largest limb sink 0.163 plus the wide mesh's own drop 0.12), so its limb stays under the meshes' horizon. Without it (sink 0.081, the dive's value) the sphere showed as a second contour 1 to 3 px above the meshes' horizon from 760 to 766, with dark dashes where the far edge of the wide mesh's matte lay on it.
- `globe.ts`: `uShow` (premultiplied presence, 1 for the orbit globe: same bytes) and `show()`; in `update` the centre is divided by the mesh scale so a scaled instance is still a unit sphere to the shader.
- `look.ts`: `under = { sink: 0.283, span: 0.45 }`.

Proof that the shell is in place: the same frame drawn both ways (`DIAG=beauty/side=orbit/noplace` against `DIAG=beauty/side=terrain`, 757, 760, 764, 771, folders s1o and s1t) shows the same ground at the same place, scale and turn.

## 01:46 to 02:10 UTC, 24 Nov: the dive side difference at T, cause and cure

- Handover report on c6bbaf6b, draft: "mercury.dive side difference at T: FAIL 99th percentile of the side difference 8 over 4". Rise sides fine (mean 0.008, 99th 0). Where: the lower left corner of 760, the ground no viewpoint saw (level 4 and the fine tile), bounded by the edge of the close picture. With the tile off still 6 over 4, so not the tile.
- Measured, in this order:
  - The corner of the globe side is the corner of the terrain side moved by 0.68 px right and 0.17 px down (phase correlation on four windows, response 0.9 to 1.06). Above the edge of the close picture both sides are equal.
  - The plan in doubles (`out/work/mercury/place/tools/sidegap.ts`, `sidegap2.ts`): ground direction of both sides for seven pixels at T: gap 6e-8 rad, 0.003 px, dive and rise alike. So the poses are right.
  - The plate coordinate `g` written out as colour through the texels view on both sides (work tree only): globe against shell 0.05 and minus 0.52 texels of level 4 everywhere in the corner. The shell is where the uniforms say (0.01 texel), the globe is not.
  - The ray from the mesh is right on both sides (0.02 px). The body normal `n` and `n * uBodyToWorld` on the globe are right (0.004 of 1/4096). After `spinY(x, uSpin)` x is off by 2.1e-5 and z by 9.2e-5.
- Cause: `spinY` took `cos(uSpin)` and `sin(uSpin)` in the shader. On the renderer of this machine the cos of 0.0445 rad is off by about 1e-4. The globe turns by `uSpin`, the shell of the terrain side has spin 0 (cos 1 and sin 0 are exact), so at T the globe's ground sat 2e-5 rad (half a texel of level 4, 0.68 px in that corner) off the shell's. It was there before; the corner was soft then, so it stayed under the limit. With level 4 and the tile sharp in that corner it shows. The rise at T has no sharp ground of the globe outside the close picture, so it passed.
- Two cures measured, both at the cause, neither softens or covers:
  - First try: `globe.ts` takes the cos and sin from the plan in doubles (`uSpin` as a vec2), no trig of the spin in the shader. Sides: dive pass (mean 0.013, 99th 1, 99.9th 2, max 17), rise pass (mean 0.003, 99th 0, max 9). But every globe frame with a spin moves by the renderer's error, the hold too: draft, master, against `base`: 615 292 px differ, largest 4 levels; 689 20736 px, largest 3; 780, 870, 959 0 px. Against `m5`: 717 165599 px (largest 13), 742 1316435 (35), 757 395949 (112), 760 0, 978 6891 (1), 985 1302782 (84), 990 1282074 (40), 1035 13770 (7). The hold may not change (MAIL 213), so this is not taken; work folder `s6`.
  - Taken: both sides run the same arithmetic. The shell of the terrain side now gets the same `uSpin` as the globe, and its mesh is turned back by the same angle in doubles (`set.ts`: `shellBase`, `shellTurn`, `spun`). In exact arithmetic nothing moves; on this renderer the shell carries the same error as the globe, so the two sides meet. `globe.ts` is as on c6bbaf6b, so no globe frame changes a byte. Sides: "mercury.dive side difference at T: pass" (mean 0.004, median 0, 99th 0, 99.9th 1, max 26; 0.015 percent over 1, 0.002 percent over 4, 2 px over 16); "mercury.rise side difference at T: pass" (mean 0.003, 99th 0, 99.9th 1, max 9; 0.008 percent over 1, 0 px over 16).
  - What is given up with the taken cure: on this renderer the ground of the globe and of the shell sits 2e-5 rad (0.68 px at master in the nearest corner at T) off the relief meshes of the close view. That was so for the globe before; it is now so for the shell after T as well (761 to 779, 960 to 976), inside the feather of the close picture. ### 03:38 UTC NOTE 501 from the Builder (to every stop builder and globe_engineer), verbatim
"A fault of the whole film, found by the first whole smooth report from the machines (Mercury, job 14): the same film frame at uhd is not the same picture as at 16 by 9 (one block differs by 45.8 levels at 713, limit 12).
CAUSE, found by mercury_builder: every globe brings its plate levels and its fine levels in by the texels of the parent a pixel of the format (uPatchFade 1.1 to 1.7 against gd * scale * size, gd from dFdx and dFdy). At uhd a pixel is half as large, so every level comes in at twice the height; at preview at half the height; in the live player it depends on the window. Brandon captures at uhd, so he gets another film than the one we judge. The term is in src/bodies/planet.ts (globe_engineer) and in the own globe code of mercury, venus, earth, jupiter, uranus, neptune and the Sun (src/stops/<stop>/globe.ts or planet.ts).
RULING (plan F: whatever blends does so by distance, height or angle): the measure is texels of the parent a 1080th of the frame height, an angle, not a pixel. In practice one factor, the height of the drawing buffer in pixels over 1080 (1 at 16 by 9, 2 at uhd, 0.5 at preview), multiplied into the density that a fade reads (parent, texels, fine, thin, cap, whatever your code calls it) and into nothing that only picks a mip for sampling.
PROOF, both by you before you name the commit: (a) at 16 by 9 the factor is 1 and every byte stays: the hashes of your own draft frames before and after are equal. (b) at uhd the picture becomes the 16 by 9 picture, only finer: npm run smooth -- --stop ID --only parity on your tree (seven frames), limits mean 12, coarse mean 3.2, one block 12, frame level 2.2.
THE SAME RULE holds for every other number in your stop that is counted in pixels and can be seen: the width of a feather, the radius of a glow, a threshold of a size on screen, a point size. If your parity is still red with the factor in, the panel names the block: find the term.
WHO: each stop builder, in the commit you name next (mercury_builder has it in work). globe_engineer: src/bodies/planet.ts and anything else under src/bodies and src/core that reads a density a pixel, as one commit on newest main (6884e80 or later), then ask me for the engine proof and say which stops draw with the shared code. saturn_coder and mars_place_builder: check your place code for the same kind of term and say what you found.

### 04:51 UTC the pixel list (MAIL 366 point 3, NOTE 501, d193): what my folders count in buffer pixels
Read from the code while the whole smooth report runs. Scaled means multiplied by `uFrame` (`frameUniform`) so that it is an angle; at 16 by 9 the factor is 1.
1. `globe.ts` PATCH_LEVELS, FINE and the globe's own texels: the density that the fade between two levels reads. SCALED in this commit (the parity cure).
2. `globe.ts` main, the silhouette: `px = fwidth(s)`; the crest's taps are `uSil.z * px` apart (look.light.silhouette.taps 1.5, floor one texel of the height map); the edge is `px * uEdge` wide (look.light.edge 1.2 times the grad factor). NOT scaled. At 4K the crest is read over half the angle (never under one height texel) and the edge is 1.2 buffer px, half the angle. Seen at the limb of the hold and of the high dive and rise. Parity 615: mean 1.424, block -2.838, so it is inside the limits; it is the 16 by 9 limb, only finer. To do: scale the taps (a look), leave the edge (an antialias) unless the Builder rules otherwise.
3. `globe.ts` main, the smear of the final tier: `move` is the shift since the last sample in buffer px; `still = smoothstep(0.5, 1.0, sm)` and `smoothstep(2.0, 6.0, sm * uJitter.z)` read it as px. NOT scaled. Only with samples above 1 in the dive and rise (the parity part renders the draft tier and does not see it). At 4K a shift of half a 16 by 9 pixel already counts as moving. `sm * fd` (the fine level's fade under smear) is texels and holds at any format. To do: `sm / uFrame` in the two thresholds, proof on final tier frames at both formats.
4. `sunplate.ts smear()`: `px = angle * height / (2 tan)`, taps `ceil(px / step)` (at most 8), the mip widened by `soft * min(px, 4)`. NOT scaled; `height` is the buffer's. At 4K the taps reach 8 at half the turn and the widening stops at 4 buffer px, half the angle. Only with a camera before this one (final tier). To do: `px / bufferFrame()` for the widening, taps stay per buffer px (they are a sampling count, not a look).
5. `set.ts`: `radiusPx` from `view.format.height`; `globe.mesh.visible = radiusPx > 0.6` is 0.6 buffer px, so at 4K the globe is drawn down to half the angle. NOT scaled. Seen only far out on the legs, under the far point (`FarPoint`, cured on main by the globe engineer in d193, takes `radiusPx` in buffer px by its own rule). `holdRadius / (radiusPx / view.format.height)` is a share of the frame height. To do: `radiusPx / bufferFrame() > 0.6`.
6. `lens.ts`, `sunplate.ts` `dFdx(uv)`, the globe's `textureGrad` calls: they only pick a mip. Nothing to scale (NOTE 501).
7. `look.ts leaveStep`, `leaveSoft`: no reader left in my folder (rg finds only the two lines). Dead values, to remove.

That holds for the frames after the seam as well as at it: across each seam with the surface view the eye's speed over its own height never dips and never turns back. At 953 + 1/2 to 955 the eye of the first bend rose almost straight up, so the whole ground moved the same way by about half a quarter pixel a capture frame: 64 to 87 percent of the ground had a fraction of 0.4 or more (19 to 24 percent in the frames round it), the left over rose from 3.2 to 4.1 for four frames and read as a pop.

### 06:13 way C, second variant (B) designed

- Hold: nothing held, `hold` null, patch-1 back to HEAD's bytes, so 615 is main's bytes by construction (to be proved on the still).

In the core the plates' weight is `given = mix(placed, G, core)`: outside the core the map's own finer ground comes by its texels as before, inside the place's own lit picture comes by height. The first place level is sampled wherever the core asks, so its picture is there at every height (minified by its mips).
- Tone: `rel` = the place's low tone over the globe's lit ground at the pixel, clamped 1/16 to 16; both sides are multiplied by `pow(rel, G)` and the plate side divided by `rel`. At G 0 the plate carries the globe's tone, at G 1 its own. The relief pits (`tilt`) are weighted by G too, so 615 and 717 hold none.
- What still changes places: inside the core the hero's craters give way to the place's, over 717 to 752 and back over the same heights in the rise. Slower than before (8 frames carry at most about 0.4 of it, before all of it), not gone.

Mail from handover_engineer (/root/handover_engineer), 03:43 UTC, low priority, word for word:
"From handover_engineer, 03:43 UTC 26 Nov. No answer needed. The crests of a relief (design (c), MAIL 1184 point 4) are named to /root: agent/engine-crest 451b726422d68229d2a4c6cde0f6c4912c1e8683 (main cd069015 merged in; four files on it: src/terrain/crest.ts, src/terrain/relief.ts and two test files). Not on main yet; do not build on it before /root takes it. Off unless your stop gives the numbers. Where to switch it on is yours (MAIL 1184), per crest. It is proved on Mars only; nothing of Mercury was drawn with it.

What it does: a layer's mesh draws a step of its distances as a wall, and from a moved eye the wall is drawn out with the picture's texels (the teeth on Mars's lit crest, 2668). A layer you name draws the cells of such a step as a near sheet over a far sheet, each rigid with its own ground, cut where you say the near side's paint ends.

The key, in the relief's motion (beside `mesh`): `crest: [{ layer, step, walk, under, out, boxes, at }]`, one entry a layer.
- layer: the name as in the files (relief-NAME-color.jpg).
- step: the least step of the inverse distance (1 over the relief's unit) between the two ends of a ramp.
- walk, under, out: in cells of the layer's mesh. walk: how far a ramp may reach from a texel to either end (a slope wider than that is no step). under: how far the far sheet goes on under the near side (as far as your worst eye draws the two sides apart). out: how far the near side's paint reaches beyond the step's middle, 0 to 1.
- boxes: [left, top, right, bottom] as shares of the layer's own box; a crest is cut only inside a box. Left out: the whole layer.
- at: points [x, y] as shares of the layer's own box, each on a crest: the step within one cell of the point, as far as it runs unbroken. Left out: every step (do not: name the crests you have looked at).

The numbers that passed at review on Mars's layer L1 (scratch, never committed), as a start: step 0.002, walk 2, under 4, out 0.7, one box, two points. Measured there on the lit crest's edge: 2668 from 5 jumps and rms 2.00 px to 0 jumps and rms 0.62; 2672 from 4 jumps (largest 10 px) to 2 (2 and 3 px, no tooth) and rms 0.70; the hold 2580 the same by eye (largest difference 27 steps).

Limits you have to know before you choose:
1. The fill under the near side is the texel of the ramp's far end, drawn out along the way across the step. A speck in the paint there becomes a streak (seen on Mars: a red mark of 12 by 8 px beside the crest).
2. Where a crest ends (a box ends it, the step runs out, no point names what goes on) both sheets lie on the mesh's own ground beyond the end and the cut runs straight on along the crest's line. At the one end I have looked at nothing shows at 10 to 1 at review and six draft frames in a row are steady. A crest that leans, or turns by less than two thirds of a right angle within a cell, is one crest, no end.
3. A crest that runs up to the layer's rim (the matte's edge) is to be ended with a box before the rim, or its fill shows past the rim.
4. Two named crests within a few cells of one another get one another's distances: name one. A second step within a cell of the first is one ramp with it.
5. A step whose near side is outside the matte is a rim, not a crest: it rides with the far side. No fill is put under a texel that is not opaque.
6. One entry a layer, so the crests of a layer share step, walk, under and out.
7. Where you have cut a crest into a layer of its own with ground painted behind it, that stays (MAIL 1184); do not name such a crest.

Pictures (Mars): agent/engine-handover-looks b792924f98e1ae810f77645e4b81fdb65199e803 (review) and 499007e293b75a3eebe77af1d2e21806508eac13 (a dive strip at draft). Ask me for a draft of your frames with your numbers if you want one before you commit."
